as_read: Small positive trials at 2 to 5 g/day and a meta-analysis finding limited effect on lipids and weight; none tests a 500 mg extract, and none named a primary outcome in its abstract.

quote.text: Yerba Maté consumption may demonstrate favorable effects on glycemic control, though its impact on lipid profiles and weight management appears to be limited.

proposed_decision_text: All three labels are Explosive Energy Metabolizer formulas printing Yerba Mate leaf extract at 500 mg among 12 to 17 active rows, with endurance, energy, metabolic or cardiovascular purposes. The stored trial 26408319 gave capsules at 3 g/day to 30 adults with obesity and reported lower body fat mass, percent body fat and waist-hip ratio against placebo, but its abstract names no primary outcome and its amount is six times the label. 29117073 gave 5 g daily to 11 trained cyclists and improved time trial performance, and 28809814 gave 2 g to 12 active women and raised fat oxidation; neither names a primary outcome, and both use amounts well above the label. 25562195 gave yerba mate tea at 5 g/day for blood viscosity, a purpose these labels do not carry. 33374524 gave an encapsulated dry extract providing 580 mg of caffeoyl quinic acid derivatives daily and found no significant effects of treatment, but its abstract gives no extract mass, so it can't be placed near the label amount, and it names no primary outcome. 35807800, a pilot in ten men, found no change in muscle strength with no dose in the abstract. The meta-analysis 41244043 reports glycemic signals from two trials in pre-diabetes and no significant effect on lipids, fasting glucose, waist or BMI, with no single dose. The review 36647770 rates risk of bias high in 22 of 32 studies. These reads are of abstracts only, and an abstract that names no primary outcome counts against qualifying for no credit.
stop_list: Fields can't hold the extract-mass gap: trials print gram amounts of leaf or tea or amounts of chlorogenic acids, labels print 500 mg of extract, and no source gives a conversion.
clinician_items: 41244043: adverse events included mucosal irritation, insomnia, tachycardia, angina, headache and gastrointestinal discomfort.
34173816: an Ilex paraguariensis infusion decreased iron absorption in hereditary hemochromatosis patients, from the title only; abstract not read in full.
29117073: resting plasma adrenaline rose with yerba mate (P = 0.002); these labels are multi-stimulant energy formulas.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_weak rests on one 30-person trial at 3 g/day, and the record's material_form says standardized leaf extract while the abstract says only Yerba Mate capsules.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. Search returned 39, 25 listed. 25562195 and 40263915 were cut at 1500 characters. 40263915 is mate tea, three servings daily. Left unread: combinations 34357081, 31994278, 26612980; chocolate or green tea arms 28935146, 27223302, 30660196; infusion trials 39708247, 26917157, 35121062, 34173816; RA review 41470797; appetite review 31126562; and the cancer association papers 29909900, 38689010, 29490609, which a clinician may want for safety.
